analysis: Docs-only PR; no source or control code changed. Two changes examined. (1) docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md adds a head-side section (lines 130-153) on an unregistered GLM sparse-state candidate. It states that SSD prefix-cache eligibility defaults on for the locally selected `EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp` via `PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel`, that `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` opts out, and that GLM stays outside registered coordinator serving models. The text says reuse requires a protected native binding, a verified encrypted restore path and charged ownership. This is consistent with T-041, whose SSD tier is default-on for eligible CBv2 models with encrypted DBK3 files, HMAC lookup tags, scope-folded salt and a 30-minute TTL. It would widen the at-rest and TTFT surface (SEC-035) to one more model. It is documentation of a source change not supplied here, so the claimed gating (verified identity, encryption, cacheSalt scoping) cannot be confirmed. T-041's detection_hint says loosening the production gate needs review. T-041 and prefix-cache.md do not yet enumerate GLM among the default-on models, which is a possible model-list drift to reconcile. (2) docs/architecture/security/encryption.md (patch hunk at head lines 107-118) documents that ad hoc signed builds get no persistent cache key and SSD stores are refused with `key_unavailable` unless an ephemeral key is allowed. It also documents a DEBUG-only `DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE` that derives the KEK from a 0600 operator-created file, not the Secure Enclave, and says release builds do not contain this path. This is an honest weakening of the SE-rooted KEK chain assumed in T-041 (c), limited to DEBUG/qualification. The claim that release builds exclude the path depends on `SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift` compile guards, which are not supplied. A later pass should verify the `#if DEBUG` gating and that the T-041 KEK posture is noted. No concrete regression is established from docs alone.
